title: Tech Architect: MERN | SaaS | AWS/Azure
description: Role: Tech Architect: MERN | SaaS | AWS/Azure Multi-Tenant SaaS Platform: MVP to General Availability Role Summary The Tech Architect owns the technical design of the SaaS platform and its path from a working MVP to a live, production product. The role decides the architecture, sets engineering standards, writes and reviews critical code, and holds the team to them. It is accountable for the platform’s structure, not for running every workstream: specialist roles (data, AI/ML, DevOps, security, QA) implement within the architecture this role defines. Key Responsibilities Multi-tenant architecture: Design the tenant model, tenant isolation, rate limiting and quotas, horizontal scaling and cost model; choose between monolith, modular monolith and microservices. API and service design: Define versioned REST/GraphQL APIs , service boundaries, event-driven patterns ( Kafka/RabbitMQ ) and data models across MongoDB, SQL and Redis . MVP to production: Decide what to reuse vs. re-architect; set production standards (error handling, logging, monitoring, tests, performance); own readiness reviews, load testing, go-live, rollback and post-launch support. MERN leadership: Lead MongoDB , Express , React and Node.js development; set front-end and back-end standards; write and review production code. Cloud architecture: Define the AWS/Azure target architecture, deployment topology and CI/CD approach (blue-green/canary, Docker, Kubernetes); DevOps/SRE implements infrastructure as code and observability. Identity and extensibility architecture: Design per-tenant SSO (SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth2, SCIM), RBAC, public APIs, webhooks, SDKs and a versioned, sandboxed plugin model. Security architecture: Set defense-in-depth design (gateway, WAF, authN/Z, encryption, secrets, audit logs); lead threat modelling and design reviews. The Security Specialist runs testing, compliance and vulnerability management. AI-assisted engineering: Introduce agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code) with review standards, guardrails and CI quality gates for AI-generated code. Technical leadership: Approve high-level designs, guide low-level designs, maintain architecture decision records and documentation, mentor senior engineers, run proofs of concept, and partner with product on trade-offs. Required Qualifications 10–15 years in software engineering, including 3+ years as an architect. Strong hands-on MERN; AWS or Azure; Docker, Kubernetes and CI/CD. Proven track record taking an MVP/POC to a live, production SaaS product. Multi-tenant SaaS, subscription billing, distributed systems and microservices; Kafka/RabbitMQ, SQL/NoSQL, Redis, object storage. SSO and enterprise authentication; security architecture (OWASP Top 10, secrets management, tenant isolation). Demonstrable use of agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code); LLM basics (RAG, tool calling). Awareness of SOC 2, ISO 27001 and GDPR; clear communication; experience leading architecture reviews. Preferred / Added Advantage Developer ecosystem or marketplace design; zero-trust, mTLS, SAST/DAST, SIEM; usage-based billing; MCP and LLM agents; Terraform/CloudFormation; SRE practices; cloud, TOGAF or security certifications. Pay: ₹2,500,000.00 - ₹3,500,000.00 per year Work Location: In person

Instead of writing every line by hand or working ticket by ticket, Builders direct AI agents to design, code, test and operate software, and are accountable for checking that the result is correct and safe in production. Builders grow along a four-level career framework. Levels reflect scope, independence and how much leverage someone gets from AI, not years of experience: Level 1: delivers well-defined work using AI tools, with coaching. Level 2: independently builds and runs AI agents and automated workflows for their features. Level 3 (Senior): sets technical direction for a product area; designs the testing, evaluation and safety checks that keep AI-built software reliable. Level 4 (Expert): shapes how AI-first engineering works across the whole organization. Every Builder is also assessed on five core competencies: Ownership, Delivery Reliability, Continuous Learning, Customer Orientation, and Communication & Collaboration. This role leads a team of Builders and is expected to operate at Level 3 or above. WHAT YOU WILL OWN 1. Product delivery, AI-first Own your product's engineering outcomes: what ships, at what quality, and how fast. Run delivery AI-first, in short cycles rather than two-week sprint rituals. Move an existing engineering team to the Builder way of working: assess each person against the framework, set clear development paths, and act decisively where someone isn't making the shift. Coach each person on the five core competencies, and grow Builders from one level to the next.
